A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and relocated equations, tables and figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original POPE experiments comparing decoding methods, forced distribution adjustments and standalone plausibility constraints, including prediction analyses and appendix results.

after.justification: v3 retains these experiments and adds results on other benchmarks in Tables 4 and 6, plus a diffusion-noise case study in Appendix C.

M1.justification: Prompt-Based Adjustment, the probability-threshold rule for Output Layer Modification, and the standalone plausibility constraint remain unchanged. The VCD, ICD and SID formulations are retained, with their detailed descriptions moved to Appendix A.

E1.justification: v3 expands evaluation beyond POPE object-presence questions on COCO, AOKVQA and GQA to MME, CHAIR, Nocaps and LLaVA-Bench. This introduces broader discriminative and generative tasks. Appendix C also adds an object-counting example under progressively corrupted visual inputs.

E2.justification: ICD is removed from the corresponding greedy-decoding comparison in Table 1, which now contains Greedy, VCD and SID. ICD remains in the sampling comparisons. The expanded benchmark evaluations introduce no new comparison algorithm.

E3.justification: v3 adds greedy and direct-sampling evaluations with MME-P/MME-C, CHAIR-S/CHAIR-I and additional generation scores, plus a noise probe at diffusion timesteps 0, 100, 300 and 500. F1 reporting is removed from two main POPE tables but retained in appendix tables. These additions do not establish changes to the retained POPE experiments.

E4.justification: v3 adds a single-image sensitivity case showing responses under increasing diffusion noise (Figure 7) and extends the existing constraint-only ablation to other benchmarks (Table 6). The earlier output-skew and prediction-transition analyses are retained, including the heatmaps moved into the main text.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. The added results continue the existing point-value reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 4 and 6 add substantial non-POPE results. For example, v3 reports greedy-decoding CHAIR-S scores of 21.6 for Greedy, 25.4 for VCD and 24.9 for SID; under sampling, the standalone constraint changes CHAIR-S from 23.2 to 22.4. Shared POPE scores remain unchanged, while some F1 entries and the Table 1 ICD results are removed.

T1.justification: The decoding distributions, plausibility constraint and output-adjustment equations remain mathematically equivalent after relocation and notation cleanup. No new theorem, proof or formal assumption is introduced; Appendix C supplies an informal mechanism explanation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same two-factor explanation of misleading gains and the same claim that contrastive decoding fails to meaningfully mitigate hallucinations. The title makes object hallucinations explicit, while the additional benchmarks support the existing thesis.

C2.justification: Appendix C adds a causal account in which perturbations obscure visual details and semantic-grounding failures undermine the linguistic-prior explanation of hallucinations. Section 5.1 also interprets the new results as restricting benefits to discriminative tasks biased toward No. These substantially extend the earlier interpretation centered on POPE response balancing and sampling.

D1.justification: v3 newly supplies a source-code link in the abstract and identifies the model and diffusion timesteps used in the new case study. Section 5.2 also explicitly lists QwenVL, which was already represented in v1's results. The new benchmark tables do not identify which listed backbone their scores summarize.

R1.justification: v3 adds references on open-ended contrastive decoding, CHAIR, Nocaps and a multimodal-model survey, while removing several general model references, including Alpaca and Llama 3. The central positioning against VCD, ICD and SID remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The technical methods section becomes a summarized Preliminary section, with detailed formulations moved to Appendix A and the POPE introduction integrated into the preliminaries. Existing appendix material moves into the main text, and the decoding-strategy comparison moves into Appendix D. The title, terminology and several explanatory passages are also revised.

P2.justification: The paper changes from a two-column to a single-column layout, redraws the constraint and adjustment diagrams, and relocates the output-skew heatmaps. It adds two benchmark tables and the perturbation figure. Main POPE tables lose F1 columns and revise their delta annotations; existing decoding results are also redisplayed within Figure 4.

improvement.justification: The new non-POPE evaluations and constraint-only comparisons address v1's narrow empirical basis, providing useful evidence about generation and hallucination beyond binary object-presence questions. The code pointer also improves reproducibility information. However, the new tables leave backbone identification unclear, and Appendix C calls the same four-fruit answer both hallucinatory and correct. These shortcomings limit the net improvement.
